rationale: Four major actionable findings across three review lenses: (1) the timezone Controller is nested inside the cronExpression Controller's render prop — the spec shows a sibling pattern and nesting causes re-registration overhead on every cronExpression change with potential field-value loss; (2) the FilterOption cast in settingsUIConfig.ts uses `as unknown as` to bypass TypeScript's structural check, masking a real type incompatibility the spec does not authorize; (3) datasource-type-specific create/update paths (Git, SVN, Google Doc, Jira, Xray, AzureDevOps) may build payloads independently of getBaseRequestFields() and therefore silently omit timezone; (4) the spec-required default-value behavioral tests for useEditPopupForm (browser timezone on create, defaults.timezone on edit) were not added. Nine additional candidates were dismissed or deferred as either spec-authorized design choices, false positives from diff summarization, or low-risk items for a SPA context.

findings.title: Nested Controller causes unnecessary re-registration of timezone field on every cronExpression change
findings.problem: The timezone <Controller name='timezone'> is rendered inside the render prop of <Controller name='cronExpression'>. React Hook Form re-instantiates the inner Controller on every render triggered by cronExpression, causing repeated field registration and unregistration. The spec explicitly shows a sibling Controller pattern where the timezone Controller sits at the same JSX level as cronExpression, not nested inside its render prop.
findings.impact: Re-registration on every cronExpression keystroke/change; potential transient loss of the timezone form value during rapid input; non-standard React Hook Form usage that increases cognitive overhead for future maintainers.
findings.recommendation: Refactor to a sibling Controller pattern: place both Controllers at the same nesting level and pass both field bindings into a single CronScheduleInput. Alternatively extract an inner wrapper component that uses useController for both fields so neither Controller's render prop contains the other.

findings.title: Double-cast `as unknown as` in settingsUIConfig.ts bypasses TypeScript structural compatibility check
findings.problem: `getIANATimezoneOptions() as unknown as { value: string; label: string }[]` forces TypeScript to accept the value without verifying that FilterOption is structurally compatible with the credential config's expected option type. The spec shows `options: getIANATimezoneOptions()` without any cast. The need for a double-cast indicates a real type mismatch that is being suppressed rather than resolved.
findings.impact: If FilterOption carries additional required fields absent in the config's option shape (or vice versa), downstream CredentialFields rendering may silently produce incorrect behavior. The cast makes the incompatibility invisible at compile time, removing the protection TypeScript provides.
findings.recommendation: Read the full FilterOption type definition and the credential config's expected options type. Either (a) widen the credential config's options type to accept FilterOption[], (b) add the missing fields to the mapping, or (c) explicitly project: `getIANATimezoneOptions().map(o => ({ value: o.value, label: o.label }))`. Remove the double-cast entirely.

findings.title: Spec-required behavioral tests for useEditPopupForm timezone defaults not present
findings.problem: The spec requires useEditPopupForm.test.ts to cover two behavioral cases: (1) timezone defaults to getBrowserTimezone() on create, and (2) timezone defaults to defaults.timezone on edit. Only schema validation tests were added to useEditPopupForm.validation.test.ts. The file the spec targets was not modified and the two required behavioral tests do not exist anywhere in the diff.
findings.impact: The timezone defaulting logic — getBrowserTimezone() on create, defaults?.timezone ?? getBrowserTimezone() on edit — is entirely untested. A regression (e.g. defaults?.cron_expression spread accidentally clobbering timezone, or getBrowserTimezone() returning empty string) would pass CI undetected.
findings.recommendation: Add tests to useEditPopupForm.test.ts (or the validation test file if project convention puts all hook tests there) covering: (a) the create-path default value equals getBrowserTimezone(), (b) the edit-path default value equals defaults.timezone when present, and (c) the edit-path falls back to getBrowserTimezone() when defaults.timezone is absent.

findings.title: Datasource-type-specific create/update paths may not spread getBaseRequestFields() and therefore omit timezone
findings.problem: The timezone field was added to getBaseRequestFields(). However Git, SVN, Google Doc, Jira, Xray, and AzureDevOps datasource types have dedicated create/update functions in useCreateIndex.ts that may build their API request payloads independently rather than spreading getBaseRequestFields(). If any of these functions do not spread that helper, timezone is silently omitted from the payload for that datasource type.
findings.impact: Timezone selection would appear to work in the form UI but not be transmitted to the backend for the affected datasource types. The server defaults to UTC regardless of the user's selection, making the feature silently broken for non-FILE datasources.
findings.recommendation: Audit every create/update call site in useCreateIndex.ts. For each datasource type function that does not spread getBaseRequestFields(), add `timezone: values.timezone || undefined` explicitly. Add at least one integration or unit test asserting that the timezone field is present in the API payload for a non-FILE datasource type (e.g. Git or Confluence).
